verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā kassapagotto kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Kassapagotta was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā kassapagotto divāvihāragato aññataraṁ chetaṁ ovadati.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Kassapagotta, having withdrawn for his day’s meditation, tried to advise a nimrod.

verses.pali: Atha kho yā tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmantaṁ kassapagottaṁ saṁvejetukāmā yenāyasmā kassapagotto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ kassapagottaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the deity haunting that forest approached Kassapagotta wanting to stir him up, and recited these verses:
It’s a waste of time to advise him, mendicant;
he strikes me as an idiot.
Even if you lit ten lamps
and brought them to him, Kassapa,
for he has no eyes to see.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā kassapagotto tāya devatāya saṁvejito saṁvegamāpādīti.
verses.english: Impelled by that deity, Venerable Kassapagotta was struck with a sense of urgency.
